problem: End-to-end mapless open-vocabulary ObjectNav policies overfit small simulator datasets (HM3DSem has 216 scenes), so they fail on unseen categories and collide often. The fragile hard DAgger-to-PPO switch also hurts training, and hybrid methods need depth and odometry.
motivation: Real-world deployment favours lightweight, RGB-only, mapless policies that generalize to free-form categories. An open-vocabulary segmentation mask of the goal can carry the open-vocabulary knowledge, so the policy does not need to learn category semantics from little data. Noisy predicted masks then need special adaptation.
key_idea: Feed a binary goal-segmentation mask (from open-vocabulary YOLOE) into a small transformer policy, and train it with an entropy-gated DAgger/PPO mixture (EALM), an auxiliary mask-reconstruction loss and a mask-area semantic reward.
insight: The goal mask is the main driver of unseen-category generalization: val unseen SR goes from 20.2 (EALM only) to 26.7 with mask+seg loss, 36.9 with mask+semantic reward, and 44.7 with all three. The semantic reward and seg loss are complementary, each alone is much worse than the two together. Predicted-mask fine-tuning teaches the agent trajectories where YOLOE can segment the target, lowering the false negative rate (68.5 to 61.3), and per-category confidence calibration mainly cuts false positives. Mask-only input gives 12.6 SR, so text is still needed, while text-only with zero mask gives 0.1 SR.
method: Goal mask encoder: a ResNet9 encodes the binary target mask into a 128-d embedding, concatenated with frozen SigLIP RGB (768-d) and text (768-d) embeddings and a 32-d previous-action embedding.

Transformer policy: a 4-layer, 8-head, 512-d decoder-only LLaMA-style transformer over the last 100 observation embeddings, with a linear action head and critic head (~130M parameters in total, 34M for the state encoder).

EALM: the PPO weight is λ_t = clip((H_high − EMA entropy)/(H_high − H_low), 0, 1) with H_low=0.35, H_high=0.75 and EMA α=0.95, and BC gets 1−λ_t; this gives single-stage, automatic DAgger→PPO transition.
Auxiliary segmentation loss: a DCGAN head reconstructs the current goal mask from the transformer feature, trained with Dice+BCE, which speeds up early representation learning.
Semantic reward: sparse success reward +2.5 and a collision penalty, plus 0.5·(clip(Δgeodesic distance) + clip(Δgoal-mask pixel area)).

Adaptation to predicted segmentation: train 200M steps with GT masks, then fine-tune 15M steps with pure PPO on YOLOE masks. Per-category YOLOE confidence thresholds are calibrated and redundant synonyms removed from the vocabulary.

setting.backbone: Frozen SigLIP encoders + ResNet9 goal-mask encoder + 4-layer transformer (trained); YOLOE (pretrained, YOLOv8-L) for masks
setting.training_data: HM3D-OVON train split in Habitat: 200M steps of DAgger+PPO (EALM) with GT masks, then 15M steps PPO fine-tuning on YOLOE predicted masks; DAgger teacher is an A* frontier-exploration planner with GT map
setting.observation: monocular RGB only (360x640, 42° HFOV) + text goal + previous action + binary goal mask from YOLOE
setting.action_space: discrete: stop, forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, look up/down 30°; 500-step horizon
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT map/GPS only for the DAgger teacher during training; GT masks used in training only)

results: On HM3D-OVON val unseen OVSegDT reaches 44.7 SR / 20.6 SPL with RGB only, beating Uni-NaVid (39.5/19.8), MTU3D (40.8/12.1, uses depth and odometry) and DAgRL+OD (37.1/19.8), and gaining +26.4 SR over DAgRL (18.3). Seen and unseen performance are nearly equal (43.6 vs 44.7 SR). EALM alone needs 200M steps versus 300M for DAgRL and gives better SR/SPL.
limitations: Depends on the quality of the external segmentation model; the false negative rate is still ~61% and GT masks give 69.3 SR, a large gap.
Predicted-mask fine-tuning raises collisions (20.2 to 45.4), and the real robot shows risky behaviour near the goal.
Cannot follow free-form text instructions, only category goals; real-robot evaluation is only qualitative demonstrations.
